description: **The UK's single largest spending department** — ~30% of total managed expenditure. HQ Caxton House (Tothill Street SW1). Created 8 June 2001 by merger of Department of Social Security (DSS) + Employment Service. Responsible for welfare + State Pension policy + delivery across GB (NI has a parallel Department for Communities scheme). Operates Jobcentre + service-centre network + ALBs (HSE · MaPS · TPR · PPF · NEST). Tier A sub-entries cover the specific programmes (State Pension · UC · PIP · DLA · Carer's · Attendance · WFP · ESA) — this is the dept parent.
notes: **WFP means-test (Sept 2024)** was highest-profile welfare change of Labour's first Budget — saves ~£1.4B/yr · ~10M pensioners lost universal entitlement · Age UK JR refused. **Carer's Allowance earnings-cliff overpayments scandal (2024)** — thousands prosecuted for marginal breaches · Kendall commissioned independent review. Ongoing legal action over PIP mental-health descriptor changes. **State Pension age review** commissioned July 2025. Permanent Secretary Sir Peter Schofield has led DWP since January 2018, making him one of the longest-tenured Whitehall perm secs; Katie Farrington serves as 2nd Perm Sec covering Disability, Health and Pensions. The department sponsors nine ALBs including HSE (health and safety regulator, ~£230M budget), TPR, PPF, MaPS and NEST. Labour's 'Get Britain Working' White Paper (Nov 2024) and 'Pathways to Work' Green Paper (March 2025) are the defining Kendall-era policy drives, alongside the commissioned Keep review of Carer's Allowance overpayments.

description: COFOG category aggregate for old-age pension spending. NOT a single programme — it sums up everything DWP pays to support pensioners under UK COFOG classification 10.2. The OSCAR £143B line under DWP captures 6 sub-programmes. Click individual sub-lines for specific programme detail (State Pension, New State Pension, Pension Credit, Winter Fuel Payment, etc.).
notes: **COFOG 10.2 is the biggest DWP COFOG category — ~48% of DWP's £297B total**. State Pension alone is the single largest line of public spending in the UK. **WASPI** controversy (PHSO March 2024 compensation recommendation → Labour REJECTED 17 December 2024 → political firestorm) sits across the sub-programmes. **Winter Fuel Payment means-testing** (July 2024 Reeves decision · partial U-turn June 2025 with ~£35k threshold restoring ~9M pensioners) is one of the largest domestic policy reversals of the 2024-29 parliament. **Pension Credit take-up gap** cascades: means-testing WFP to PC-linked eligibility in 2024 tied the WFP saving to the same ~37% non-take-up that already denies HB entitlement to eligible pensioner renters. **SPA timetable**: 66 → 67 starts April 2026 (complete April 2028) · 68 by 2046. Triple-lock cost escalation has been a recurring fiscal-risk focus for OBR and IFS since the 2011 introduction. COFOG 10.2 'Old age' follows UN SNA 2008 / CoFoG 1999 definitions — covering cash benefits and services for loss of income or autonomy in old age. UK spending at ~5.2% of GDP is BELOW the EU27 average of ~10.4% and OECD average of ~7.7% (Eurostat 2022, OECD Pensions at a Glance 2023), reflecting the UK's relatively low Basic/New State Pension replacement rate (~25% vs OECD ~51%) offset by private occupational pensions not counted in this COFOG. Direct OECD comparison requires SOCX framework which adds occupational layers. Line is AME + demand-led, forecast by OBR; biggest recent revision = triple-lock-driven 8.5% uprating April 2024.

description: England's third-largest spending department. Funds schools (via LAs and academy trusts), SEND provision, early years, 16-19 education, apprenticeships, higher-education regulation, student loans, and teacher pensions. Money reaches schools through two channels: Dedicated Schools Grant ring-fenced to LAs, and ESFA direct grants to academy trusts (now 82% of secondary pupils, 42% of primary).
notes: Scope note: the £140B OSCAR line is total DfE departmental spending including student loan outlay scored via the RAB charge — not all of this is cash spending in the public-perception sense. Biggest story: IFS Annual Report on Education Spending 2024 found **real-terms per-pupil funding in state schools only returned to its 2010 level in 2024-25** — a lost decade. **SEND financial crisis**: NAO (Oct 2024) branded the system 'financially unsustainable'; LA DSG deficits ~£3.2B cumulative with the statutory override expiring March 2026 and no replacement policy. The **98% SEND tribunal overturn rate** is repeatedly cited by the Education Select Committee as evidence LAs routinely refuse statutorily-owed support. **Plan 5 student loans** (Aug 2023) cut the threshold £27,295→£25,000 and extended the term 30→40 years — IFS calculated this shifts ~£2.3B/year from taxpayers to graduates, hitting middle earners hardest (regressive relative to Plan 2). **Ruth Perry Prevention of Future Deaths report (7 December 2023)** by the Senior Coroner for Berkshire found that Ofsted's inspection 'likely contributed' to the headteacher's death; Ofsted's **single-phrase overall-effectiveness judgements were abolished on 2 September 2024**. University sector stress: OfS May 2024 found ~40% of English HE providers forecast a deficit in 2024-25, compounded by the January 2024 dependant-visa ban collapsing international postgraduate numbers. Bridget Phillipson heads DfE under Labour with a ministerial team including Catherine McKinnell (Schools), Stephen Morgan (Early Education), Baroness Jacqui Smith (Skills) and Janet Daby (Children & Families); Susan Acland-Hood has been Permanent Secretary since September 2020. The **Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill** (introduced Dec 2024) is the defining Labour education legislation — mandating academy trust accountability, a Unique Pupil Identifier, and ending 'free schools' default for new openings. ESFA is being wound up into DfE core (March 2025) and Skills England launches April 2025 to replace IfATE.

description: The 206 NHS trusts that actually deliver care across England — hospitals, mental-health, community, specialist, and ambulance services. Collectively employ ~1.35 million FTE and run ~163,000 beds. Their funding flows from NHS England via the 42 Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) that replaced 106 CCGs in July 2022.
notes: Elective waiting list peaked at 7.77M (Sept 2023) — the defining political issue. Sector moved from ~£1.4B underlying deficit (2022-23) to a planned ~£2.2B deficit for 2024-25; ~60% of trusts in deficit at year-end 2023-24. Provider workforce grew ~20% since 2019 but productivity remains below pre-pandemic (Health Foundation). Under Labour, Wes Streeting as Health Secretary commissioned the **Darzi Investigation** (final report Sept 2024) which described the NHS as 'broken' and set up the 10-Year Health Plan. On 13 March 2025 Streeting announced NHS England's abolition — functions to return to DHSC over two years, with Sir Jim Mackey taking over as transitional CEO from Amanda Pritchard (who resigned February 2025). Dr Penny Dash replaced Richard Meddings as NHS Chair in October 2024. The **Elective Reform Plan** (Jan 2025) targets returning to the 18-week referral-to-treatment standard by March 2029.

description: Contributory pension paid to individuals who have reached State Pension age with sufficient NI contributions. Two systems run in parallel: the 'new' State Pension (for those reaching pension age after 6 April 2016, full rate £221.20/week) and the 'basic' State Pension (for earlier cohorts, £169.50/week plus additional SERPS/S2P).
notes: WASPI — 1950s-born women had their State Pension age raised from 60 to 66 with inadequate notice. PHSO recommended £1,000–£2,950 compensation each (March 2024) for ~3.6M affected women. Government rejected the scheme in December 2024, sparking ongoing backlash. The triple lock itself — guaranteeing annual uprating by the highest of CPI, earnings, or 2.5% — cost DWP an extra ~£9B in the April 2024 uprating. State Pension has the lowest fraud+error rate of any major DWP benefit — 0.1% fraud / 0.4% error per DWP F&E Bulletin 2023-24. However the **LEAP underpayments exercise** has already paid £1.46B to 119,000 women (as of Feb 2025) for historic underpayments affecting married-woman, widow and over-80 categories. State Pension is **fully reserved** across the UK (not devolved) — identical DWP State Pension paid in Scotland, Wales and NI, though devolved governments run top-ups (Scotland's Winter Heating Payment replaced WFP from winter 2023-24). Age rises legislated: 67 by Apr 2028, 68 by 2044-46; next statutory review commissioned July 2025.

description: The commissioning arm of the NHS in England — NHS England, the 42 Integrated Care Boards, primary care (GPs, pharmacy, dentistry), medicines, Continuing Healthcare, and central DHSC policy. This line is the money *before* it reaches hospital trusts: the £130.8B 'NHS Provider Sector' branch (the 206 trusts) is tracked separately to avoid double-counting.
notes: Scope note: the OSCAR £83B line is DHSC *net* of the Provider Sector branch — the full DHSC group headline is £181.7B (HM Treasury Main Estimates 2024-25). Biggest current story: **NHS England abolition**, announced by PM Starmer and Health Secretary Wes Streeting on **13 March 2025**. NHSE is merging back into DHSC over ~2 years, with a combined headcount cut of ~50% (~9,000–10,000 posts). It is the biggest NHS commissioning reorganisation since the 2012 Lansley reforms that established NHSE in the first place. The Institute for Government, King's Fund and Nuffield Trust all warned this absorbs management bandwidth precisely when waiting lists and productivity need focus. Resident-doctor strikes ran 44 days through 2023-24; the September 2024 deal (~22.3% over 2 years) closed that dispute but a new 2025-26 ballot reopened it. The **Leng Review (July 2025)** on Physician Associate scope of practice recommended renaming to 'Physician Assistant' and pausing expansion. Under Labour, Wes Streeting leads DHSC with junior ministers Karin Smyth (Health), Stephen Kinnock (Care), Ashley Dalton (Public Health, from January 2025 after Andrew Gwynne was removed over WhatsApp controversy), and Baroness Merron (Mental Health/Patient Safety in Lords). Samantha Jones is Interim Permanent Secretary from December 2024 after Chris Wormald moved to become Cabinet Secretary. DHSC sponsors ten major ALBs including MHRA, NICE, CQC and UKHSA. The department is managing the largest machinery-of-government restructure in NHS history following the March 2025 announcement to abolish NHS England and re-integrate its functions into DHSC.

description: HM Treasury's accounting bucket for cash flows to non-government bodies where HMT acts as sovereign backstop. In 2024-25 dominated by **quarterly indemnity payments to the Bank of England's Asset Purchase Facility (BEAPFF)** covering BoE's losses on unwinding the QE gilt portfolio. Smaller flows from Covid loan-guarantee calls (BBLS/CBILS/CLBILS), energy Supplier-of-Last-Resort costs (Bulb), UK Asset Resolution runoff (Northern Rock / Bradford & Bingley legacy), National Wealth Fund capitalisation, and Ukraine ERA loan commitments. Line was near-zero in pre-2020 OSCAR vintages — exploded with Covid + QT reversal.
notes: **CRITICAL SCOPE NOTE**: Exact £ decomposition of the £71B is NOT published in any single public table — the ~£28-30B APF-in-2024-25 estimate is a differenced figure from the cumulative £85.9B since October 2022. Treat as estimate. **The APF indemnity is scored as AME spending, not as debt interest in the National Accounts** — should NOT double-count with the separate Debt Interest Payments tree line. Sanity check against ONS PSF 'Interest payable' (MF6U series). **Truss mini-budget Sept 2022** triggered BoE's emergency gilt-buying (via APF) that stabilised the LDI crisis — those gilts are still being unwound under QT, generating the losses this bucket covers. **BBLS fraud scandal**: NAO £4.9B fraud estimate + Lord Agnew resignation January 2022 over fraud-control failures. **Bulb SoLR**: the hand-over to Octopus is under PAC scrutiny over whether the repayment structure captures true value. **Treasury Committee 2024** questioned whether the Bank's active gilt-sales pace is taxpayer-optimal given faster unwinding crystallises losses sooner. **G7 context**: US Fed remittances to Treasury also went negative (deferred asset) in 2022-23, but the UK's APF indemnity is structurally unique (cash-settled, not accrual-deferred). Critics argue this COFOG 4.1 line is a catch-all that obscures what is effectively a monetary-policy flow inside fiscal accounts. HM Treasury owns this line with Chancellor Rachel Reeves and Chief Secretary Darren Jones as political leads; delivery routed via the Bank of England's BEAPFF Ltd SPV (for APF indemnity) and UK Government Investments (shareholder stake management). NAO's September 2023 QE report set out the cumulative taxpayer cost trajectory of ~£130B net over the programme lifetime (OBR March 2024 EFO). description: The UK's economics and finance ministry — sets fiscal policy, controls public spending across all departments, manages tax strategy, oversees financial-services regulation, and manages the national debt via the Debt Management Office. **Scope note**: the £63.5B OSCAR figure INCLUDES the annual debt-interest bill (~£105-122B on different bases). HMT's standalone operating footprint is closer to £6B DEL. The separate 'Debt Interest Payments' Tier A card covers the gilt-interest side in detail — don't double-count.
notes: **Truss-Kwarteng mini-budget crisis**: 23 September 2022 'Growth Plan' announced £45B of unfunded tax cuts (top-rate abolition, NI reversal, stamp duty cuts) with no OBR forecast published. 30-year gilt yield rose ~120 basis points in three sessions; sterling hit record low $1.035. LDI (liability-driven investment) pension schemes faced margin calls on interest-rate swaps triggering a forced-selling doom loop in long-dated gilts. On 28 Sept, BoE launched a temporary targeted gilt-buying facility up to £65B capacity (actual purchases ~£19.3B) to stabilise LDI funds. Kwarteng sacked 14 Oct; **Truss resigned 20 Oct — shortest-serving PM in UK history (49 days)**. Hunt reversed virtually all measures by 17 Oct but higher debt-service bill was baked into forward curves (~£20-30B extra over the medium term). **Index-linked gilt shock 2022-23**: RPI peaked at 14.2% October 2022. Because ~25% of gilts are RPI-linked, coupons and principal auto-uplift — OBR estimated **~£50B of additional debt-interest crystallised in 2022-23 alone** from the inflation spike. This is why UK debt interest rose faster than any other G7 country's. **Oct 2024 Budget fiscal rule reform**: Chancellor Reeves switched the debt target from PSND to PSND ex-BoE (excludes APF/QT losses; counts illiquid financial assets) — creating ~£50B of additional investment headroom. The IFS Green Budget 2024 makes the case that debt-interest 'crowding out' is the binding fiscal constraint. NAO and Treasury Select Committee have questioned the pace of BoE's active gilt sales (QT) given realised-loss crystallisation. HM Treasury is the UK's oldest department (Exchequer 1126 → Commissioners of the Treasury 1714). Sir James Bowler has been Permanent Secretary since October 2022, with Cat Little as 2nd Perm Sec and Head of Government Finance Function. Rachel Reeves became the UK's first female Chancellor on 5 July 2024, with Darren Jones as Chief Secretary (Cabinet-rank), James Murray as Financial Secretary, and Emma Reynolds as Exchequer Secretary (from Jan 2025 replacing Tulip Siddiq). HMT **owns the Barnett formula** and Statement of Funding Policy — Scotland ~9.7%, Wales ~5.7%, NI ~2.9% population shares of comparable English-departmental DEL changes. Sponsors OBR, UKDMO, UKGI, IPA, NS&I and the Royal Mint.

description: Central-government spending on interest and indexation uplift on gilts (UK government bonds) and National Savings & Investments products. Issuance and secondary-market operations are handled by the Debt Management Office (DMO), an HM Treasury executive agency established in 1998.
notes: 2022-23 index-linked uplift alone contributed ~£50B of that year's record £111B debt-interest bill because RPI peaked at 14.2% (Oct 2022). BoE Bank Rate rose from 0.1% (Dec 2021) to 5.25% (Aug 2023). Quantitative Tightening (active gilt sales) since late 2022 realises losses on APF gilts indemnified by HMT — ~£100B lifetime cost (OBR). IFS (2024) warns debt interest is 'crowding out' public services — now exceeds schools and defence combined. Largest single line of AME expenditure outside social protection. Three main drivers: stock of debt, effective interest rate (Bank Rate + term premia), and RPI/CPI (index-linked accretion). DMO holds remit to minimise long-run cost subject to risk, mainly via diversified-maturity gilt issuance. Bank of England Asset Purchase Facility (APF) quantitative tightening since 2022 adds indirect cost to HMT. Sinking-fund proposals raised by IFS 2024 for long-term debt reduction rejected by HMT as inflexible. 2024 Mansion House + Budget confirmed ~£290B gilt remit for 2024-25. Policy ownership sits with HM Treasury, while the UK Debt Management Office (an HMT executive agency created in April 1998) runs gilt auctions and cash management. Beneficiaries are gilt holders: roughly 30% overseas investors, 25% UK pension and insurance funds, 20% UK banks and building societies, 20% the Bank of England via the Asset Purchase Facility, and 5% retail savers. The funding trajectory tripled from £27B in 2019-20 to a £116B peak in 2022-23 before moderating to ~£105B in 2024-25 — driven principally by index-linked gilt revaluation as CPI ran hot through 2022-23. The accounting line is continuous since the 1694 Bank of England founding, with gilt-edged securities issued under the Consolidated Fund Act 1751.

description: NHS England (operating name of the NHS Commissioning Board) is the DHSC arm's-length body that allocates funds to 42 Integrated Care Boards, directly commissions specialised + primary care, and sets national standards. Created 1 October 2012 by Health and Social Care Act 2012 to give the NHS operational independence from ministers. **13 March 2025: PM Starmer + Health Secretary Streeting announced NHSE will be abolished and merged back into DHSC over ~2 years** — biggest NHS reorganisation since the 2012 reforms that created it.
notes: **Biggest reorganisation since Lansley 2012 reforms — which NHSE itself embodied**. Rationale: re-centralise political accountability for NHS performance with ministers, end 2012's 'arm's length' settlement. Kings Fund / IfG / Nuffield Trust all warned that a 2-year reorg absorbs senior management attention during a period of record elective waiting lists (~7.4M referrals late 2024) + productivity push — comparing with the 2012 reforms' 3 'lost years'. Redundancy costs ~£50-100k per senior post (NAO 2016 methodology) — payback period on £500M/year savings likely 2-3 years before net. Pending primary legislation, NHSE continues as statutory body; functions transfer operationally first, legally later. **Accountability concern**: concerns from clinical bodies + select committees that re-absorbing NHSE into DHSC without clear operational firewall risks politicising operational decisions (waiting-list targets, service closures). **CARAN allocation fairness debate**: longstanding concern (Health Foundation) that formula under-weights deprivation vs age — 2016 ACRA refresh added health-inequalities adjustment but critics argue it's too small. **Specialised commissioning phased delegation** to ICBs since 2023-24 criticised for postcode-variation risk in low-volume services — abolition adds further structural uncertainty. NHS England operates from Wellington House (Waterloo) via 7 regional teams and 42 Integrated Care Boards (statutory from 1 July 2022). Sir Jim Mackey took over as transitional CEO in April 2025 after Amanda Pritchard resigned in February 2025 (Streeting confidence lost); Dr Penny Dash became Chair in October 2024. The Darzi Investigation (Sept 2024) described NHSE as 'over-centralised, under-powered', fuelling **Streeting's 13 March 2025 abolition announcement** — functions return to DHSC over two years with ~50% HQ headcount cut in year 1. NAO's March 2024 Workforce Plan review validated the long-term training pipeline but flagged funding gap. NHSE serves ~57M GP-registered population and ~1.5M workforce.

description: COFOG category aggregating all working-age sickness + disability cash benefits administered by DWP. NOT a single programme — bundles PIP, DLA, ESA (contributory + income-related), Attendance Allowance, Statutory Maternity Pay, Industrial Injuries, Severe Disablement Allowance. The £57.6B under DWP captures ~19% of DWP's total.
notes: **Largest reform questions in UK welfare policy** live under this COFOG. **WCA abolition planned from 2028** (Nov 2023 Conservative 'Transforming Support' White Paper · confirmed by Labour March 2025 Pathways to Work Green Paper) would end the Work Capability Assessment and **passport health-related UC top-ups from PIP entitlement instead** — triggered Labour backbench rebellion 2025 because disability groups argue PIP's mobility + daily-living descriptors miss health-only claimants who currently qualify under WCA. **PIP caseload growth**: 2.05M (2019) → 3.6M (2024, +75%) — fastest-growing working-age benefit · OBR forecasts 4.3M by 2028-29. **DLA-to-PIP migration** (2013-2019) reduced entitlement for hundreds of thousands (NAO + W&P Committee reports). **BMJ Open 2023 Barr et al. study** associated WCA reassessments with increased suicide + mental-health deterioration. **Labour's March 2025 Green Paper** projected £4-5B/year savings from tighter eligibility + WCA-to-PIP passporting — contested by Disability Rights UK, Scope, Mind, MS Society, Z2K through 2025. COFOG 10.1 'Sickness and disability' follows UN CoFoG 1999 with sub-categories 10.1.1 sickness + 10.1.2 disability benefits. 2024-25 sub-components: PIP ~£23B, DLA residual ~£7B, ESA ~£13B (falling), UC-LCWRA ~£10B, Attendance Allowance ~£7B, IIDB ~£0.7B. International: UK at ~2.0% of GDP is ABOVE OECD average ~1.8% and — crucially — rising faster than any OECD country since 2019 (OECD SOCX). Scottish devolution from 2022 replaced PIP with ADP, child DLA with CDP, and AA with PADP, with caseload phasing out of UK 10.1 as transfer completes. OBR March 2024 EFO projects ~£75B by 2028-29 driven by PIP caseload growth 3.6M→4.3M.

description: COFOG category for education spending NOT classifiable to a single educational level — dominated by the academy route (direct grant from ESFA) which spans primary + secondary pre-GCSE + post-16 in single trust structures. The £50B under DfE bundles Academies (gross £40B), Dedicated Schools Grant components that cross levels (High Needs £9.97B), and FE Skills spending. NOT a single programme.
notes: **Accounting scope note**: The gross Academies £40B + offset −£37B = NET central-gov academy spending ~£3.5B. 'Offset' is NOT a funding cut — it's the recoupment from LA DSG when a pupil moves to an academy (so same money isn't counted twice). **SEND financial crisis is the defining sub-story**: NAO October 2024 declared the system 'financially unsustainable' · LA DSG cumulative deficit ~£3.2B end 2024-25 · **statutory override keeping deficits off LA general funds expires 31 March 2026** with no replacement policy — LGIU + County Councils Network warn quarter of districts risk s114 if override expires as scheduled. **98% SEND tribunal overturn rate** repeatedly cited by Education Select Committee as evidence LAs routinely refuse statutorily-owed support. **MAT CEO pay** became political flashpoint after IfG + Observer investigations showed ~100 trust CEOs earning >£150k in 2022-23 · six trusts paid CEOs over £250k. **Wakefield City Academies Trust** collapsed 2017 · **Bright Tribe Trust** lost 10 schools 2018 · ~40 academies under DfE Financial Notices to Improve at any time. COFOG 9.5 is the 'not-definable-by-level' residual education category — in the UK it is DOMINATED by the academy-route accounting anomaly: academy schools are direct-granted from central ESFA (now DfE) rather than flowing through LA education services, so span primary+secondary+post-16 without being assignable to COFOG 9.2/9.3. This lifts UK 9.5 to ~1.7% of GDP vs OECD average ~0.4%; without the anomaly UK would be ~0.2% of GDP. Gross academy spend ~£40B is offset by ~£37B LA DSG recoupment → ~£3.5B NET central addition. ESFA abolition (March 2025) consolidates flows into DfE core; April 2025 Skills England replaces IfATE and takes over adult skills funding.  Smallest of the ten COFOG education sub-codes (09.1 pre-primary/primary, 09.2 secondary, 09.3 post-secondary non-tertiary, 09.4 tertiary, 09.5 'not definable', 09.6 subsidiary services, 09.7 R&D education, 09.8 n.e.c.). UK spend here is dominated by adult skills bootcamps, Multiply (adult numeracy, launched Sept 2022 via UK Shared Prosperity Fund), and learning-disability adult education. Labour Jul 2024 Skills England consolidation folds multiple sub-09.5 lines into single mapping exercise expected 2025.

description: Small UK Government department acting as Scotland's voice at Westminster + Westminster's interlocutor with the Scottish Government. description: The core new State Pension (nSP) expenditure line for people reaching State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016. EXCLUDES the Protected Payment top-up (separate £1.19B line that preserves pre-2016 higher entitlement). Single-tier replacement for pre-2016 Basic State Pension + Additional State Pension (SERPS/S2P). AME — demand-led, outside departmental spending limits.
notes: **WASPI remains the defining controversy**. PHSO final report (21 March 2024) found DWP guilty of maladministration in communicating 1995 + 2011 SPA changes to ~3.6M women born in 1950s · recommended compensation **£1,000 to £2,950 per woman** (Level 4 PHSO scale · total £3.5-10.5B). **On 17 December 2024 Labour government formally REJECTED the compensation scheme** — arguing most women knew of the changes and a blanket scheme would be unfair to taxpayers. Rejection triggered political firestorm, WASPI legal-action threats, sustained criticism from Labour backbenchers and cross-party MPs through 2025. **Women's NI gap issue**: ~25% of women reaching nSP age have NI gaps (often from caring years pre-HRP/credits reform), depressing entitlement despite single-tier design's intent to narrow gender gap. State Pension is a RESERVED matter — no Scottish, Welsh or NI equivalent exists; Social Security Scotland delivers disability and carer benefits only, not retirement. F&E of 0.1% (~£150M on a £46B line) is the lowest in the DWP portfolio, reflecting automated National Insurance record matching. PHSO's March 2024 WASPI finding recommended £1,000-£2,950 remedy payments per affected woman; DWP under Liz Kendall rejected blanket compensation (Dec 2024), triggering judicial-review threats from WASPI campaigners. Labour's Autumn Budget 2024 locked in the triple lock for the full Parliament — projected to add £31B/yr to the line by 2029-30 (OBR Welfare Trends Oct 2024).

key: MINISTRY OF HOUSING, COMMUNITIES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT
description: The UK central-government department that funds English local authorities (grants, not the councils' own spend), sets national housing and planning policy, and oversees building safety after Grenfell. Renamed from DLUHC to MHCLG in July 2024 under the Starmer government. Distinct from the £141.7B 'Local Government (England)' branch — that's the councils themselves; this is the money central government channels TO them.
notes: Renamed from DLUHC to MHCLG in July 2024 under the Starmer government. **Birmingham s114 (5 September 2023) is the largest council bankruptcy in UK history** — £760M equal-pay liability plus a £131M Oracle ERP implementation disaster, triggering a 21% council tax rise over two years and ~£300M in forced asset sales. LGIU's March 2024 survey found 51% of councils 'not confident' of balancing 2024-25 budgets; a quarter of district councils risk s114 by 2026 if the DSG SEND deficit statutory override expires as scheduled (March 2026). **Temporary-accommodation cliff**: London boroughs alone spend ~£4M/day on TA (up 68% in two years). LHA subsidy frozen at 2011 rates forces councils to absorb ~£700M/year gap. LHA was restored to 30th percentile in April 2024 at ~£1.2B/year cost, then **re-frozen from April 2025** after just 12 months — Crisis and Shelter estimate this will push a further 80,000 households into housing stress. **Grenfell Tower Inquiry Phase 2 Final Report published 4 September 2024** with 58 recommendations including a single construction-industry regulator. **Awaab's Law** regulations (following the 2020 death of two-year-old Awaab Ishak in Rochdale from damp/mould) commencing 2025-26 force social landlords to fix damp within strict timeframes. NAO and PAC criticised political steering of Levelling Up Fund rounds — 2022 allocations disproportionately benefited Conservative-held constituencies per IFS analysis. Real-terms council funding still ~10% below 2010 per capita despite 2024-25 Core Spending Power uplift. English Devolution White Paper published 16 December 2024 — proposes statutory strategic authorities (mayoral by default), abolition of two-tier councils in favour of unitary structures, and standing fiscal devolution for combined authorities. Pennycook driving Planning and Infrastructure Bill (2025) to mandate 1.5M homes over Parliament via NPPF revisions (Dec 2024) restoring mandatory housing targets.

description: UK department for the English transport system + reserved transport matters GB-wide. Covers rail (Network Rail infrastructure · HS2 · Train Operating Companies post-franchising) · Strategic Road Network (via National Highways) · buses · aviation (CAA) · maritime · active travel · road safety. Administers the largest single passenger-rail grant in Europe and the multi-year Road Investment Strategy. Following the Passenger Railway Services (Public Ownership) Act 2024, DfT is progressively taking TOCs back into public ownership as franchises expire — pending the full Great British Railways Bill expected in 2025.
notes: **HS2 Phase 2 cancellation (4 October 2023)** at the Conservative Party conference by PM Sunak: Birmingham-Manchester and the eastern leg scrapped; £36B 'Network North' reallocation announced for unspecified road/bus/rail schemes. PAC (Feb 2024) called HS2 'a casebook example of how not to run a major project'. Reporting alleged Sunak announced without full Cabinet sign-off — Midlands + Northern Conservative mayors (Andy Street, Ben Houchen) publicly objected. **Rail nationalisation**: Passenger Railway Services (Public Ownership) Act received Royal Assent November 2024 — **South Western Railway became the first operator transferred to the public-sector operator (DfT Operator) on 25 May 2025**. Full Great British Railways Bill expected in 2025 to consolidate track + train under a single guiding mind. **Bus £2 → £3 cap** from 1 January 2025 — a controversial Labour Budget Oct 2024 decision, extended through end of 2025. **Silvertown Tunnel** opened **7 April 2025** (tolled) — first new Thames road crossing in east London since the Blackwall Tunnel. **A303 Stonehenge tunnel**: quashed by High Court 2021, re-approved 2023, **cancelled by Labour July 2024** with ~£166M sunk costs. **Smart motorways scandal**: coroner rulings into fatalities on All-Lane-Running sections + BBC Panorama investigations drove the April 2023 cancellation; campaigners continue to call for hard-shoulder reinstatement on existing sections. **TfL Khan-Shapps feud** through 2022-24 over Covid bailout conditions, TfL capital funding and ULEZ expansion (Aug 2023) to outer London — ULEZ cited as a factor in the 2023 Uxbridge by-election. Great British Railways (GBR) Bill introduced 2025 to bring track + train under a single public body, reversing 1993 privatisation — Southeastern, LNER, Northern already nationalised; TransPennine Express, SouthWestern, c2c to follow on franchise expiry 2025-27. description: Direct-grant funding from the Education & Skills Funding Agency (ESFA) to academy trusts for primary and secondary schools up to GCSE (Key Stages 1–4, ages 5–16). Academies are state-funded schools independent of local-authority control — they get money directly from central government instead of via the Dedicated Schools Grant. About 82% of England's secondary pupils and 42% of primary pupils are now in an academy.
notes: Scope note: this node is £28.1B GROSS pre-16 direct grant. In the tree you'll also see 'DfE Grants to Academies Offset' at −£37.0B — that's NOT a funding cut; it's the recoupment from local-authority Dedicated Schools Grant so the same money isn't counted twice. When a pupil moves from a maintained school to an academy, the LA's DSG is reduced by that pupil's NFF entitlement and ESFA pays the academy directly instead. Critical controversy: **Multi-Academy Trust CEO pay** became a political flashpoint after IfG / Observer investigations showed ~100 trust CEOs earning >£150k in 2022-23; six trusts paid CEOs over £250k. The Education Select Committee (2023) called for pay restraint. Academy failures: **Wakefield City Academies Trust collapsed in 2017** after stripping ~£1M from reserves before handing schools back. **Bright Tribe Trust** lost its 10 schools in 2018 after NAO found governance failures. The regulator ESFA issues **Financial Notices to Improve (FNtIs)** to academies running deficits — ~40 active at any time. Academy freedoms over teacher pay/conditions: in theory academies can diverge from the School Teachers' Pay and Conditions Document (STPCD); in practice ~95% still follow it because they hire from the same teacher labour market. The **2022 Schools White Paper** aim of 'every school in a strong MAT by 2030' was dropped by Labour in 2024. Academy share of state-funded schools: 82% secondary, 43% primary (DfE stats Jan 2024). NAO Jan 2024 flagged 13% of secondary MATs and 24% of LA maintained secondaries running in-year deficit. Labour Jul 2024 Children's Wellbeing Bill (introduced Dec 2024) reverses some academy freedoms (QTS, pay, curriculum) while retaining structural form.

description: The grant-routing sub-line of MHCLG — principal conduit through which central government channels revenue + specific-purpose funding to England's 317 principal local authorities. Sits alongside (and is quantitatively larger than) the 'Communities' policy side. Controls Social Care Grant, pooled Better Care Fund, residual Revenue Support Grant, Section 31 pass-through grants, Levelling Up/Towns/UKSPF programmes. Does NOT control council-tax or retained business rates — those are local — but sets the rules, the settlement, and top-up grants that complete 'Core Spending Power' (CSP).
notes: **s114 contagion 2018-2023** exposed structural under-funding + risk-taking: Northamptonshire (2018) · Croydon (2020/2022/2023) · Slough (2021) · Thurrock (2022) · Woking (2023) · Birmingham (Sept 2023) · Nottingham (Nov 2023). Woking's £1.9B debt on ~£2B of commercial property is the most egregious single case; Birmingham's equal-pay liabilities (Abdulla v Birmingham CC line) + botched Oracle ERP implementation (>£100M overspend) is the largest council collapse in UK history. **Commissioners are in place** at Birmingham, Nottingham, Thurrock, Woking and Slough. **LGA, SIGOMA, County Councils Network, IFS, NAO, PAC** all repeatedly flag that grant-routing through MHCLG has been systemically insufficient to match statutory duties — especially adult social care, SEND, temporary accommodation — forcing councils into reserve-depletion and commercial risk. **Local-audit crisis**: ~99% of 2022-23 LA accounts were late as of 2024; MHCLG statutory backstop (Sept 2024 for 2022-23) forced mass 'disclaimed' opinions. **Household Support Fund**: persistently 'temporary' since Oct 2021, renewed successively in each fiscal event at £742-842M. **Cross-UK delivery divergence**: England CSP formula is cash-based + damped, Scotland GAE is needs-assessed per client-group, Wales SSA uses an indicator-based distribution, NI district councils self-fund via domestic+non-domestic rates (no equivalent grant). MHCLG Local Government Finance Directorate publishes the Settlement each Feb; Office for Local Government (Oflog) launched 2023 monitors performance but not finance. Local Audit Office proposed Dec 2024 to replace collapsed PSAA/FRC audit regime.

description: Power-sharing executive (First Minister + deputy FM from the largest unionist and nationalist parties) plus ministers allocated by d'Hondt — currently a five-party mandatory coalition (DUP, Sinn Féin, Alliance, UUP, SDLP). The 90-member Stormont Assembly funds NHS NI (HSC), schools, Invest NI, transport.
notes: The 'funding cliff edge 2026-27' is the NI Fiscal Council's warning — short-term 2024 stabilisation funding ends before the 24% needs uplift has fully accumulated under Barnett maths. Stormont uses cross-community consent and petition-of-concern mechanisms; major decisions require both unionist and nationalist majorities. NI is the only UK nation using Single Transferable Vote for its legislature. The £33.21B headline is the NI Block Grant — set by UK HMT via Barnett + 24% needs-based uplift (Interim Fiscal Framework 2024). O'Neill-Pengelly executive delivered the 2024 Public Sector Pay Framework settlement (~£600M) funded from the 2024 stabilisation package. Lough Neagh algal-bloom crisis (summer 2023 onwards) became the test case for DAERA's enforcement capacity under Minister Andrew Muir (Alliance).  Executive re-formed 3 Feb 2024 after two-year DUP boycott (Feb 2022 - Feb 2024) over NI Protocol/Windsor Framework concerns. Power-sharing history: suspended 2002-07; collapsed Jan 2017 (RHI scandal) and restored Jan 2020 via New Decade, New Approach; collapsed again Feb 2022 until Feb 2024 Safeguarding the Union deal. Labour Jul 2024 under Hilary Benn agreed £3.3B financial package incl. interim fiscal framework pegging funding to need (~124% of English per-head baseline per 2024 NI Fiscal Council analysis). Legacy Act 2023 repeal and Windsor Framework implementation dominate 2024-25 UK-NI agenda. Head of the NI Civil Service Jayne Brady is the permanent-secretary-equivalent coordinating across the 9 Stormont departments that form the ALB inventory: TEO (Executive Office), Finance, Health, Education, DAERA, DfC (Communities), DfE (Economy), Justice, and DfI (Infrastructure). The MoG lineage runs from the Belfast/Good Friday Agreement 1998 through the Northern Ireland Act 1998 to the 2006 St Andrews Agreement and the 2024 Safeguarding the Union package that ended the 2022-24 DUP boycott. Restoration on 3 February 2024 produced the first-ever nationalist First Minister (Michelle O'Neill, Sinn Féin) with Emma Little-Pengelly (DUP) as deputy.

description: Everything outside the principal councils — 43 territorial police forces (funded via PCCs or mayors), ~30 fire & rescue authorities, the Greater London Authority, 10+ Mayoral Combined Authorities, ~9,000 parishes, plus national park authorities and integrated transport authorities.
notes: Four English mayors gained 'trailblazer' single-settlement status (GM & WM in 2024; North East, Liverpool, South Yorkshire in 2025). Police precepts up £13 Band D flexibility 2024-25. PCC model criticised for low turnout (15–25% at elections). Parish precepts uncapped — Queen's Park Community Council and some town councils raising 40%+ to fund services districts have cut. 'Other Authorities' encompasses 43 territorial police forces (via PCCs/mayors), ~30 fire authorities, GLA, 12 Mayoral Combined Authorities (covering ~55% of English population), ~9,000 parish/town councils, and National Park Authorities — all sitting outside the principal council layer. The English Devolution White Paper (Dec 2024) proposes 'Mayoral Strategic Authorities' as the next model covering ~1.5M+ population catchments. Funding grew £25B→£32.4B (2021-25), ~8-9% nominal p.a., driven by police+fire pay settlements.

description: Upper-tier authorities in the surviving two-tier areas — Kent, Essex, Hampshire, Surrey, Hertfordshire, Lancashire and 15 others. Deliver the expensive people-services (social care, schools, roads, fire in some areas) while shire districts below them do housing, bins and planning.
notes: County Councils Network reports counties face £54B adult-social-care bill by 2030. Average county raised council tax by the maximum 4.99% without referendum every year 2022-25. Surrey CC abandoned its 15% referendum in 2017 under government pressure. Hampshire, Kent and Hertfordshire all issued effective-bankruptcy warnings in 2024. 21 English shire county councils (post-April 2024) deliver upper-tier services to ~25.8M people (~46% of England) in remaining two-tier areas — Kent, Essex, Hampshire, Surrey, Hertfordshire, Lancashire et al. MHCLG (Rayner/McMahon/Healey) owns the policy relationship. Funding grew £25B→£31.4B (2021-25) at ~7-8% nominal p.a., but real-terms core funding down ~11% since 2010 (CCN). Adult social care consumes ~45% of budgets; SEND transport + children's services rising fast. Surrey abandoned its unitary bid in May 2024; Hampshire is forecasting a £132M deficit for 2025-26. The **Dec 2024 English Devolution White Paper** mandates unitarisation of remaining two-tier areas within this Parliament — Phase 1 priority areas named Feb 2025 (Sussex, Essex, Hertfordshire, Kent candidates).
